Archival Dispatch: 16 Master Broadcasts Dated Across Babe Ruth, W.C. Handy Blues, Admiral Byrd Antarctica, and The Boswell Sisters

Batch 99 Forensic Discoveries

Batch 99 recovers and dates 16 monumental historical broadcasts spanning baseball history, the birth of American blues, polar exploration, close-harmony jazz vocalizing, pioneering bluegrass, science fiction radio, golden age advertising, and Broadway composition: 2 priceless Babe Ruth recordings capturing 'The Sultan of Swat' describing his legendary called home run in the 1932 World Series at Wrigley Field and addressing baseball journalists in 1948, W.C. Handy ('Father of the Blues') performing and detailing the composition of 'St. Louis Blues' on ASCAP On Parade (1944), Admiral Richard E. Byrd's live shortwave broadcasts from the ice at Little America in Antarctica during his Second Antarctic Expedition (1934), The Boswell Sisters delivering their intricate New Orleans close harmony on 'Fare Thee Well, Annabelle' (1935), Lester Flatt & Earl Scruggs with The Foggy Mountain Boys on Martha White Biscuit Time (1958), Bewley's Chuck Wagon Gang performing Western swing (1949), Elsa Miranda singing the iconic 'I'm Chiquita Banana' calypso commercial (1944), Roddy McDowall starring in the audition pilot of Chris Conway, Rocket Ranger (1952), Meredith Willson leading orchestra rehearsals (1949), Chuck Foster and His Orchestra (1945), and Jack Carson on Our Land Be Bright (1945).
